title: Relative Hom evaluation and its transport map for a family of functors
statement:
Use quasicategories, internal functor simplicial sets, coherent transformations and right-pinched mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the arrow mapping complexes $U_C(a,c)$ and right-pinch maps $j_{C,a,c}$ of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison], and the coherent Hom bifunctors and specified arrow-fibration transport of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification]. Work in a fixed universe $\mathcal W$ and a containing universe for categories of $\mathcal W$-small objects. Let $B,C,E$ be $\mathcal W$-small quasicategories, $K$ a $\mathcal W$-small simplicial set, and let
$$i:B\to C,\qquad t:B\to E,\qquad T:K\times C\to E$$
be simplicial maps satisfying the equality $T\circ(\mathrm{id}_K\times i)=t\circ\operatorname{pr}_B$ on $K\times B$. Thus the entire restriction to $K\times B$, including its higher simplices, is independent of $K$. For $b\in B$, $c\in C$, put $M_{b,c}=\operatorname{Map}_C(i(b),c)$ and let $q^T_{b,c}:A^T_{b,c}\to K$ be the pullback along $T(-,c)$ of the source-fixed arrow left fibration of $E$ with source $t(b)$. Define a map over $K$
$$\Phi_{b,c}:K\times U_C(i(b),c)\longrightarrow A^T_{b,c}$$
by the following simplex formula: if $h:\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to C$ has constant endpoints $i(b),c$ and $k:\Delta^n\to K$, its arrow coordinate is $(z,s)\mapsto T(k(z),h(z,s))$. The base coordinate is $k$.

There is a coherent natural transformation, in the infinity category of functors from $B^{\mathrm{op}}\times C$ to $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S_{\mathcal W})$,
$$\varepsilon_{b,c}:\Delta_K H_C(i(b),c)\longrightarrow H_E(t(b),T(-,c)).$$
The Hom/arrow transport comparisons can be chosen coherently in $b,c$ so that the image of $\varepsilon_{b,c}$ under the mapping-space comparison of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] is the map $\Phi_{b,c}\circ(\mathrm{id}_K\times j_{C,i(b),c})$, after identifying $H_C(i(b),c)$ with $M_{b,c}$. This is an identification in the full space of maps over $K$, with its higher homotopies, and is compatible with arbitrary simplicial parameters and pullback along maps $K'\to K$. These comparisons are compatible with enlargement of the containing universe.

In particular, for an edge $u:c\to c'$ of $C$, the naturality square has upper map $\Delta_K(u\circ-)$, lower map the coherent postcomposition transformation $H_E(t(b),T(-,u))$, and vertical maps $\varepsilon_{b,c},\varepsilon_{b,c'}$. It commutes with its coherent homotopy in $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S_{\mathcal W})$. The analogous square for precomposition along an edge of $B$ holds as well. The postcomposition square, including its transport identification, is valid for parameterized families of composable arrows and retains the data on $K\times\Delta^1$ and all higher simplices. No equivalence assertion about $\varepsilon$ or about spaces of sections is made. Empty $K$ and empty mapping spaces are allowed.

source.place: Agent-formulated relative compatibility lemma: Definition 7.4.2.2 and Warning 7.4.2.3 specify compatibility with the universal transport element, Proposition 7.4.2.6 and Corollary 7.4.2.17 compare full mapping spaces. Corollary 8.3.5.8 (046J) and Remark 8.3.5.9 (03PD) give single-functor Hom compatibility; the relative assertion above is an additional lemma, not a verbatim consequence stated there. Read online; WANTED: archived Kerodon. Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags; no Stacks tag states this quasicategorical assertion.

proof.text: For every $n$-simplex $k:\Delta^n\to K$ and every $h:\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to C$ with endpoints $i(b),c$, apply the simplicial map $T$ to $(k,h)$ and obtain $(z,s)\mapsto T(k(z),h(z,s))$. Its source endpoint is $t(b)$ by $T\circ(\mathrm{id}_K\times i)=t\circ\operatorname{pr}_B$, and its target is $T(k(z),c)$, so it is a simplex of the pullback source-fixed arrow left fibration defining $A^T_{b,c}$. The base is $k$. Restriction along every simplex operator in $\Delta$ commutes with this formula, so these assignments define the stated simplicial map $\Phi_{b,c}$ over $K$; this is the degreewise expansion of the internal-functor and pullback definitions.

source.place: Definition 7.4.2.2 and the simplicial formula for the source-fixed arrow left fibration

proof.text: The coherent mapping bifunctor supplied by space-valued transport is functorial in both variables, including all higher simplices. For each $k$ it sends an arrow $\alpha:i(b)\to c$ to $T(k,\alpha):t(b)\to T(k,c)$. Because the restriction of $T$ to $K\times B$ is the displayed constant map, the source of this arrow is independent of $k$ and the assignments for all $k$ assemble into a coherent transformation $\varepsilon_{b,c}:\Delta_KH_C(i(b),c)\to H_E(t(b),T(-,c))$. Applying the same construction to simplices in $B^{\mathrm{op}}\times C$ proves coherent naturality in $b,c$; no vertexwise replacement is used.

source.place: Theorem 7.4.2.4 and Remark 7.4.2.5, with the Hom-functor compatibilities of Subsection 8.3.5

proof.text: Use the transport classification for the source-fixed arrow left fibration of $E$: its pullback along $T(-,c)$ is precisely $q^T_{b,c}$, while the constant functor with value $H_C(i(b),c)$ is represented by $K\times H_C(i(b),c)\to K$. The mapping-space comparison in that classification therefore sends $\varepsilon_{b,c}$ to a map over $K$ from the constant representative to $A^T_{b,c}$. Under the mapping-space identification $H_C(i(b),c)=M_{b,c}$, the right-pinch comparison sends an $n$-simplex to its arrow simplex on $\Delta^n\times\Delta^1$. Evaluating this arrow by $T$ gives exactly $(z,s)\mapsto T(k(z),h(z,s))$, hence the resulting map over $K$ is $\Phi_{b,c}\circ(\mathrm{id}_K\times j_{C,i(b),c})$. The equality holds in every degree, so it is an identification of full mapping spaces with their higher homotopies.

source.place: Proposition 7.4.2.6 and Corollary 7.4.2.17, compared with Corollary 8.3.5.8 (046J) and Remark 8.3.5.9 (03PD)

proof.text: The comparison in the preceding step is coherent in $b,c$ because the transport node makes its mapping-space equivalence coherent in both functors and the pinch node makes $j$ natural under every simplicial functor. Thus a simplex of $B^{\mathrm{op}}\times C$ carries to the corresponding simplex of maps over $K$, not merely to an equality of vertices. If $r:K'\to K$, pulling back $q^T_{b,c}$ and the displayed formula along $r$ replaces $k$ by $r k$ and commutes strictly with both sides; the pullback clauses of the two cited classifications give the same conclusion. Enlarging the containing universe leaves the formulas and these identifications unchanged.

source.place: Remark 7.4.2.5 and Proposition 7.4.2.6, parameter and universe naturality

proof.text: For an edge $u:c\to c'$ of $C$, transport in the second variable sends $\alpha:i(b)\to c$ to $u\circ\alpha$, while the family $T$ sends it to $T(k,u)\circ T(k,\alpha)$. The simplicial functor identity $T(k,u\circ\alpha)=T(k,u)\circ T(k,\alpha)$ makes the square with upper map $\Delta_K(u\circ -)$, lower map $H_E(t(b),T(-,u))$, and vertical maps $\varepsilon_{b,c},\varepsilon_{b,c'}$ commute degree by degree. The same calculation on a simplex of the parameter gives the specified coherent homotopy, and the transport comparison identifies it with the corresponding square of maps over $K$.

For an edge of $B$, transport in the first variable acts by precomposition: an arrow $v:b'\to b$ sends $\alpha:i(b)\to c$ to $\alpha\circ i(v)$ and sends the target-side arrow through $t(v)$. The equality on $K\times B$ gives $T(k,\alpha\circ i(v))=T(k,\alpha)\circ t(v)$, so the analogous precomposition square commutes on every simplex. This proves the asserted $B$-naturality together with its higher coherent homotopies.

source.place: Hom-functor precomposition compatibility in Subsection 8.3.5 and Definition 7.4.2.2

proof.text: If $K$ is empty, the constant representative and every map over $K$ are the unique empty simplicial maps, so the construction still gives the claimed transformation. If a mapping space or a fiber is empty, the formulas define maps of the corresponding possibly empty simplicial sets and do not require a chosen point. None of the preceding steps asserts that $\varepsilon_{b,c}$ or a section space is an equivalence; they establish only the displayed identification and naturality, as required.
